claim: Describes Merlin LOX/RP-1 gas-generator propulsion, aluminum-lithium tank skins, fault-tolerant avionics, payload interfaces and verification requirements.
scope: A customer guide does not release internal source code, complete CAD, or flight-qualified model parameters.

claim: The 17 March 2015 testimony describes Raptor as LOX/methane with a full-flow staged-combustion cycle.
scope: Historical architecture statement; future-facing performance claims are not current measured specifications.

claim: The assessed vehicles are primarily stainless steel, and thermal tiles primarily silica.
scope: An assessed configuration envelope is not a specific flown vehicle; no certified material-property tables are supplied.

claim: The FAA index links assessments and decisions for cadence, trajectories and contingency reentry.
scope: Environmental review does not establish a specific flight license or demonstrated performance.

claim: The final EIS evaluates up to 44 annual launches with associated infrastructure scenarios.
scope: Assessed capacity is not demonstrated cadence; no vehicle license follows automatically.

claim: NASA describes collaboration with SpaceX on a tiled PICA-derived Dragon heat shield and Ames arc-jet qualification.
scope: Does not publish PICA-X formulation or a complete material-property dataset.

claim: Discloses antenna-module packaging involving an antenna element, cavity, PCB coupling and amplifier arrangement.
scope: Disclosure does not prove use in a product. Legal-status summaries are not a freedom-to-operate analysis.

claim: The 9 January 2026 order authorizes a second tranche of 7,500 Gen2 satellites, totaling 15,000 authorized Gen2 satellites, subject to conditions.
scope: Authorized count is not deployed or operational count; later orders may supersede conditions.

claim: Describes user phased arrays, gateway antennas and laser terminals, with brightness-mitigation design tradeoffs.
scope: Manufacturer disclosure is not independent effectiveness validation or a current V3 specification.

claim: The retrieved Mini sheet specifies an electronic phased array, 110-degree field of view and 25–40 W average consumption.
scope: Mini-specific specification, not a satellite antenna design or an internal schematic.

claim: The 14 March 2024 Flight 3 account identifies hot staging and an internal-tank cryogenic transfer demonstration.
scope: Internal transfer is not ship-to-ship refueling; preliminary test events do not supply calibrated fluid coefficients.

claim: NASA states that SuperDraco combustion chambers in the May 2015 pad-abort demonstration were 3D printed.
scope: Does not establish that every engine component is printed or disclose manufacturing process settings.

claim: Demo-1 included autonomous ISS docking with approach and retreat maneuvers.
scope: No docking control law, perception code, or complete test telemetry is released.

claim: A sampled vertical PD model can demonstrate a numerical contact case under chosen parameters.
scope: Own code, synthetic inputs and checked equations; not physical validation.

claim: A simulation workbench should precede a digital-twin claim until real-asset synchronization exists.
Published optimal-control methods can be reconstructed as a separate academic study.
scope: Implementation planned; published formulation is not SpaceX flight software.
